markets.rules_primary: If a bill repealing or ending at least one of Donald Trump's tariffs, also passed by the House in identical form, has passed the Senate after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation that would repeal, terminate or nullify, in full, at least one tariff imposed by Donald Trump in either of his terms. A tariff is the duty set by one proclamation, executive order or trade-agency action, such as the Section 232 steel tariffs, the Section 301 forced-labor tariffs or the Section 338 tariffs on Canada. A joint resolution qualifies only if it ends such a tariff. Ending a tariff in full means for every product and country it covers: a bill ending all Section 338 tariffs on Canada qualifies, while a bill that only exempts certain products or countries, lowers a rate, delays or suspends a tariff, refunds duties already paid, or requires congressional approval of future tariffs does NOT qualify.

The same measure must pass the full House and the full Senate in identical form after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules or a discharge petition, and the market resolves to Yes when the second chamber passes it. Passage includes agreeing to the other chamber's amendment or adopting a conference report. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying repeal. Passage by only one chamber, committee approval, and a rule providing for consideration do NOT count. The market resolves regardless of any presidential signature, veto or veto override.

markets.rules_primary: If a bill or constitutional amendment imposing term limits on Supreme Court justices has passed the House after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying measure is legislation that would impose a fixed term or a maximum length of service on justices of the Supreme Court, such as an 18-year term followed by senior status or retirement. It may apply to future appointees only. A joint resolution proposing a constitutional amendment qualifies, and it passes the House only if it receives the two-thirds vote required to propose an amendment. Legislation limited to ethics, recusal, or the size of the Court does NOT qualify.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains qualifying term limits. Committee approval, a rule providing for consideration, or a discharge petition reaching 218 signatures without passage does NOT count. Senate passage, enactment and ratification do NOT count.

Legislation that changes only the Court's jurisdiction, procedures, ethics rules or term limits, adds seats to lower courts, or proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Court's size does NOT qualify.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. markets.rules_primary: If a bill banning mid-decade congressional redistricting has passed the House after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation that prohibits states from carrying out more than one congressional redistricting between decennial census apportionments, meaning a state that has redistricted after an apportionment may not redistrict again until after the next apportionment. An exception for redistricting required by a court, the U.S. Constitution, a state constitution or the Voting Rights Act, approved in a statewide referendum, or carried out by an independent commission, does not prevent a bill from qualifying, and a bill qualifies whether it applies to current maps or only to future decades. The Redistricting Reform Act, the TRUST Act, the RESET Act, the Save American Democracy Act or a successor bill with the same effect qualifies. Legislation that only sets map-drawing criteria, requires independent commissions, regulates redistricting litigation or requires transparency, without barring a second redistricting in the same decade, does NOT qualify.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying ban. Committee approval, a rule providing for consideration, or a discharge petition reaching 218 signatures without passage does NOT count. Senate passage and enactment do NOT count.

markets.rules_primary: If a state law recognizing both gold and silver as legal tender is enacted in Tennessee before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law.

Standard legislation requiring executive approval: final passage by all required legislative bodies, executive signature OR becoming law despite executive inaction OR successful veto override, and satisfaction of any required waiting periods
Legislation not requiring executive approval: final passage and completion of required waiting periods
Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.

Tax exemptions for purchases or sales of gold and silver, by themselves, do NOT qualify.

markets.rules_primary: If a bill requiring private employers to use E-Verify has become law after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation that mandates that an employer that is not a governmental entity, federal contractor or vendor use E-Verify, or a successor federal electronic employment-verification system, to verify at least one employee. A mandate backed by a penalty for not using the system qualifies, and a mandate that phases in after Jan 1, 2028 qualifies once the bill becomes law. A law that requires recipients of federal grants, loans or other federal financial assistance that are not governmental entities to use E-Verify qualifies.

It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as enacted contains a qualifying mandate.

The following do NOT qualify:
A bill that only extends, reauthorizes or funds E-Verify without requiring employers to use it
A bill that only encourages voluntary use of E-Verify or only studies it
A bill that only requires E-Verify for governmental entities, federal contractors or vendors

Executive action and state laws do NOT count.

markets.rules_primary: If legislation granting legal status to Dreamers has become law after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A Dreamers legal-status law is legislation that grants legal status to a class of people who are present in the United States without lawful status and who entered as minors, whether named the Dream Act, the American Dream and Promise Act, the Dignity Act, or anything else.

Legal status means protection from removal together with work authorization, or conditional or lawful permanent residence. Any age-at-entry or presence-date cutoff counts. A broader legalization law that also covers this group qualifies.

A private bill, Temporary Protected Status, Deferred Enforced Departure, DACA through executive action or a court ruling, parole, and changes to visa numbers or visa categories do NOT qualify.

It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as enacted contains a qualifying provision. Committee approval or passage by one chamber does NOT count.

markets.rules_primary: If a Dreamer bill has passed the House after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A Dreamer bill is legislation that grants legal status to people on the basis that they entered the United States as minors and are present without lawful status, such as the American Dream and Promise Act, the Dream Act or the Dignity Act. Legal status means protection from removal together with work authorization, or conditional or lawful permanent residence. Broader legalization that covers this group also counts. Legislation that grants status only to other groups, such as Temporary Protected Status or Deferred Enforced Departure holders or agricultural workers, a private bill, and a simple or concurrent resolution do NOT qualify, even if some people covered entered as minors.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules or a special rule. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying provision. Committee approval, or a rule providing for consideration without passage, does NOT count. markets.rules_primary: If a bill expanding the federal child tax credit has passed the House after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation that expands the federal child tax credit under section 24 of the Internal Revenue Code by raising the maximum credit per child, making more of the credit refundable, or widening who is eligible for it, whether temporary or permanent and whether in one step or phased in over time. The American Family Act or a successor bill with the same effect qualifies. Legislation that only extends or makes permanent current law, only adjusts the credit for inflation, or only changes other credits, such as the earned income tax credit or the child and dependent care credit, does NOT qualify.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying expansion. Committee approval, a rule providing for consideration, or a discharge petition reaching 218 signatures without passage does NOT count. Senate passage and enactment do NOT count.

markets.rules_secondary:
Advanced AI chips are items covered by the U.S. advanced-computing export controls, such as ECCN 3A090 and 4A090 and their .z and successor classifications.

Verification may be of a product's location or of its non-diversion to a restricted destination, by any method, including audits, inventories, attestations or technical controls.

A qualifying provision may be part of a broader law, and a statute directing an agency to impose the requirement qualifies on enactment, even if implementation comes later.

Laws that only require a study or report without requiring verification, only authorize an agency to impose a requirement, or apply only to chips that stay in the United States do NOT qualify.

markets.rules_primary: If a bill imposing a federal tax on billionaires has passed the House after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation that imposes a new federal tax on the net worth, or on the unrealized gains, of billionaires, meaning individuals whose net worth or assets exceed a threshold of at least $1 billion. The Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act, the Billionaires Income Tax Act or a successor bill with the same effect qualifies. Legislation that only raises existing tax rates, changes capital gains, estate or inheritance rules, taxes loans or corporations, or applies a wealth tax that starts below $1 billion does NOT qualify.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying tax. Committee approval, a rule providing for consideration, or a discharge petition reaching 218 signatures without passage does NOT count. Senate passage and enactment do NOT count.

markets.rules_secondary: The designation refers to the Department of War's supply-chain-risk designations of Anthropic under 41 U.S.C. 4713 and 10 U.S.C. 3252. A waiver or modification that permits such use for some Department of War programs or contractors qualifies, as does an official Department of War or White House authorization permitting any Department of War component or contractor to use an Anthropic AI model in Department of War work, even if a designation otherwise remains in effect. An action that permits use only by civilian federal agencies does not qualify. A court ruling alone does not qualify unless the Department of War or the White House officially announces an action that permits such use.

markets.rules_primary: If a bill regulating AI in political ads has passed the House after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation with a provision specific to political advertisements, other election communications or AI depictions of candidates that requires, or directs a federal agency to require, a disclaimer, label or other disclosure of AI-generated or materially AI-altered content, or that prohibits or restricts distributing materially deceptive AI-generated content of candidates or campaigns, including fraudulent misrepresentation of them. The REAL Political Advertisements Act, the AI Transparency in Elections Act, the Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act, the AI Ads Act, or a successor bill with the same effect qualifies. Legislation that only requires a study or report, only mentions AI, applies to AI-generated content or digital replicas generally (such as general AI labeling, voice and likeness rights or intimate-image bills), or only addresses information about when, where, how or who may vote, or depictions of election officials, does NOT qualify.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying provision. Committee approval, a rule providing for consideration, or a discharge petition reaching 218 signatures without passage does NOT count. Senate passage and enactment do NOT count.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if any component becomes impossible to occur (resolving to No) or all components have been satisfied (resolving to Yes).
markets.rules_primary: If ALL of the following occur: Iran deal: Agreed, WTI: Below $60, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For all outcomes in this market, Iran deal is “Agreed” if the “Before Jan 1, 2028” market of the US-Iran nuclear deal event resolves to Yes and “Not agreed” if it resolves to No, using that event’s definition of a new Iran-US nuclear deal and its clarifications. WTI refers to the settlement price of WTI Crude Oil on Dec 31, 2027 at 2:30 PM ET, based on the February 2028 contract released on Dec 31, 2027.

This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No. Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset: Iran deal (AGREEMENT), WTI (WTIDIR). A component is satisfied when its outcome matches the stated condition, so Iran deal: Not agreed is satisfied if AGREEMENT resolves to No, and the contract resolves to No as soon as a qualifying deal occurs. All stated bounds are inclusive. For example, “$60 to $74.99” includes both $60.00 and $74.99, “$90 or above” includes $90.00, and “Below $60” means below $60.00.
markets.title: Will a US-Iran nuclear deal be agreed before 2028 AND WTI settle below $60 on Dec 31, 2027?

custom_strike.Combo: Trump's approval rating drops below 35% + Democrats win control of the House of Representatives + The U.S. enters a recession + The U.S. unemployment rate is at least 5% in 2026

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if any component becomes impossible to occur (resolving to No) or all components have been satisfied (resolving to Yes).
markets.rules_primary: If ALL of the following occur: Trump's VoteHub approval rating drops below 35% in 2026 AND Democrats win control of the House of Representatives after the midterms AND the U.S. enters a recession between Q4 2025 and Q4 2026 (inclusive) AND the U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) is at least 5% in any month in 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No.

Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset:

"Trump's VoteHub approval rating drops below 35%" uses POLLINGAPPROVALINPERIOD
"Will Democrats win control of the House of Representatives?" uses CONTROL
"Will the U.S. enter a recession?" uses NBERRECSS
"Will the U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) be at least 5%?" uses ECONSTAT

For economic data releases, resolution uses the first officially released value (not preliminary or revised estimates unless specified). All conditions must be satisfied within the specified time period.

Additional specifications:

POLLINGAPPROVALINPERIOD - the threshold need only be met once during the period
CONTROL - based on the Speaker of the House on Feb 1, 2027
NBERRECSS - requires two consecutive quarters in which the most recent estimates of seasonally adjusted annualized percent changes of quarterly US real GDP are negative

markets.rules_primary: If Drake performs (or it is announced that they will perform) at Lollapalooza Chicago 2027 during the official event timeframe, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Additional clarification(s):

Drake appears on stage or in the official broadcast or stream; AND

Drake actively and perceptibly contributes to a musical performance by singing (including audible lead or backing vocals), rapping, playing a musical instrument, DJ-ing, or conducting a live band; AND

Is either a scheduled performer, a guest appearance during another artist's set, or is formally announced as a performer by official event organizers or Drake's official representatives.

Note: This Contract may resolve on the announcement of Drake’s anticipated performance at Lollapalooza Chicago 2027. If an announced Drake later withdraws from Lollapalooza Chicago 2027, this will not affect the resolution of the Contract.

The following constitutes a performance and IS encompassed by the Payout Criterion:

A full solo performance of one or more songs.

A collaborative or joint performance in which Drake is physically present and actively contributes musically.

A guest appearance during another artist's set in which Drake performs at least one full verse, chorus, or musical segment.

A medley in which Drake is present and actively performing, even if Drake's portion is partial.

A performance in which Drake performs entirely via an officially produced and sanctioned satellite feed, video link, or holographic display that is presented as part of the official live event program, provided that the performance is real-time or was produced specifically for and presented exclusively within Lollapalooza Chicago 2027.

A DJ set in which Drake is the performing DJ operating equipment live, regardless of whether Drake sings.

A pre-recorded performance segment presented as part of the official event program, provided it is attributed to Drake by the official event organizers and presented as a performance (rather than a tribute, retrospective, or archival clip).

A performance that begins within the official event timeframe but extends beyond it due to scheduling overrun, provided the performance commenced during the official timeframe.

A performance at a rescheduled version of Lollapalooza Chicago 2027 where the reschedule occurs within one year of the original event date, pursuant to the postponement provisions below.

markets.rules_primary: If the US federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse of appropriations for at least 1 day between Jan 1, 2027 and Dec 31, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A shutdown is defined as the government's orderly suspension of agency work that is not legally excepted, typically accompanied by furloughing the employees who perform that work, when funding is unavailable.

Shutdown status is recorded at 10:00 AM ET each day. Partial shutdowns are included. A shutdown lasting "at least X days" requires the shutdown to be in effect at 10:00 AM ET on X+1 consecutive days. For example, if a shutdown is first in effect at 10:00 AM ET on October 1, 2026, and remains in effect at 10:00 AM ET on October 2, 2026, the shutdown has lasted at least 1 day.

Examples that would count toward the shutdown day count:

OMB releases a formal directive that orders heads of the affected agencies to "execute plans for an orderly shutdown," which is in effect as of 10:00 AM ET on the relevant date
OPM posts a current operating status that indicates that "due to a partial lapse in appropriations, Federal Government operations vary by agency"
During an ongoing shutdown, OPM posts a status referencing an Executive Order excusing employees for a holiday, but does not indicate the government has resumed normal operations

Examples that would NOT count toward the shutdown day count:

A technical lapse in appropriations occurs, but OMB directs agencies to continue standard operations
Government closures or operating status changes resulting exclusively from Federal holidays, inclement weather, or other emergencies, unless such closures coincide with a shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations

A shutdown that began before Jan 1, 2027 counts for the days it is in effect from Jan 1, 2027.

markets.early_close_condition: This market may close early following the governing NCES IPEDS Admissions release for fall 2026.
markets.rules_primary: If Brown (IPEDS Unit ID: 217156) has the lowest admissions rate among all Ivy League schools for the fall term of 2026, the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Important Information:
The admissions rate of an institution is its total number of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students admitted divided by its total number of first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate applicants for the fall term of 2026.
The admissions rate is determined from the first public release by the National Center for Education Statistics of Admissions component data for the fall term of 2026 that is designated as provisional (or, if the Source Agency no longer uses that designation, the first public release not designated as preliminary or early release data). 
If multiple qualifying institutions are tied for the lowest admissions rate, “Yes” positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied institutions, and “No” positions will pay 1 minus the "Yes" payout.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of continuing resolutions for fiscal year 2027 that become law is at least 2 before October 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A continuing resolution is a law providing continuing appropriations for any part of the 12 regular fiscal year 2027 appropriations areas. Each law counts once, however many areas it covers and however long it runs.

Counts toward the total:

A government-wide continuing resolution
One covering only some areas, or only specific programs and activities
A full-year continuing resolution
One enacted after a lapse in appropriations has begun
One enacted as a division of a broader law

Does NOT count:

A regular fiscal year 2027 appropriations act
A supplemental appropriations act
Continuing appropriations that do not cover fiscal year 2027

The count ends once all 12 regular fiscal year 2027 appropriations acts are law. A temporary government-wide extension does not end it. If all 12 never become law, the count is final on October 1, 2027.

For fiscal year 2025 the applicable number is 3, the last of which funded the remainder of that year.

markets.rules_primary: If SNS-backed candidate wins the next Serbian presidential election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
SNS-backed candidate: Any presidential candidate nominated or formally endorsed by the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) before the Republic Electoral Commission's candidate-nomination deadline for the first round.

Student-backed candidate: Any presidential candidate nominated or formally endorsed, before that deadline, by the proposer of the student-designated electoral list in the October 25, 2026 parliamentary election, provided that candidate is not also nominated or endorsed by SNS.

For presidential or direct elections, the candidate who wins according to the electoral system (electoral college, popular vote, or runoff as applicable) and either (i) is inaugurated/sworn in/takes office, or (ii) the scheduled inauguration date passes without a different candidate taking office, is the winner.

This market is eligible for accelerated resolution by a consensus of media calls. See full rules for details.

The three parties count whether they run in a coalition or separately. A district seat won by a coalition candidate counts for the party to which the INE attributes it. Later changes of party by a deputy do not count.

markets.rules_primary:
If the Oregon Department of Forestry reports that timber volume harvested from Board of Forestry Lands in fiscal year 2027 is above 

160 million board feet, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Fiscal year 2027 runs from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

Resolution will use ODF’s reported BOF Timber Harvest Volume for FY2027. Only timber actually harvested from Board of Forestry Lands will count; timber merely planned, offered, or sold but not harvested during FY2027 will not count. Volume is measured in million board feet (MMBF).

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if certified election results are published.
markets.rules_primary: If the margin of victory for Chiang Wan-an in the 2026 Taipei mayoral election is at or above 2%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The margin of victory is the vote share received by Chiang Wan-an minus the vote share received by the candidate that finishes immediately behind Chiang Wan-an if Chiang Wan-an wins, or the candidate that finishes first if Chiang Wan-an loses. If Chiang Wan-an wins, the margin will be positive; if Chiang Wan-an loses, the margin will be negative; if Chiang Wan-an ties for first place, the margin shall be 0.

Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound, and no rounding shall be applied. For example, for consecutive ranges of 5-6% and 6-7%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 5-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-7% range. If Chiang Wan-an runs under multiple parties or is listed multiple times, votes attributable to the same underlying candidate will be summed.
markets.title: Will the margin of victory for Chiang Wan-an in the 2026 Taipei mayoral election be at least 2%?

markets.rules_primary: If, as of the end of Nov 16, 2026, a hemp-derived beverage enclosed in a 12-fluid-ounce container that contains exactly 3 milligrams of naturally produced delta-9 THC (and no other cannabinoids) is treated under federal law as lawful to sell, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Underlying for this Contract evaluates the federal legal status of a beverage that:

is enclosed for retail sale in a single sealed 12-fluid-ounce (355-milliliter) container;
contains exactly 3 milligrams of tetrahydrocannabinol in that container, all of which is delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol naturally produced by, and derived directly from, a Cannabis sativa L. plant qualifying as hemp under 7 U.S.C. § 1639o as in effect on January 1, 2025, and none of which is synthesized or manufactured outside the plant; and
contains no tetrahydrocannabinolic acid, no other cannabinoid of any kind, and no other substance listed in any schedule of the Controlled Substances Act.

The market resolves to Yes if, as of the end of Nov 16, 2026, at least one of conditions (a) through (d) is satisfied: 

(a) Statutory and regulatory status: Under the federal statutes and federal regulations in legal effect, the beverage is not a controlled substance in any schedule of the Controlled Substances Act. 
(b) Judicial relief: One or more orders of a federal court of the United States are in full force and effect that bar the enforcement of the amendments made by Section 781 of Public Law 119-37, or of the CSA’s treatment of the beverage as a controlled substance, with respect to the entire class of products and with effect throughout the United States. 
(c) Funding prohibition: Enacted federal legislation prohibits the use of federal funds to implement, administer, carry out, or enforce the amendments made by Section 781, or the Controlled Substances Act, with respect to the retail sale of the beverage throughout the United States. 
(d) Express authorization: Enacted federal legislation expressly authorizes or makes lawful the retail sale, in interstate commerce, of the beverage.

Only statutes, regulations, and court orders in legal effect as of the end of Nov 16, 2026 shall be considered. None of the following, standing alone, is sufficient to resolve to Yes: State, local, territorial, and tribal laws; Federal enforcement discretion, deprioritization policies, or non-binding agency guidance; Proposed rules; Federal court orders granting relief limited to particular parties, plaintiffs, products, sellers, or geographic areas; Funding prohibitions that have lapsed or expired; and Regulation of the beverage under any body of federal law other than the CSA (e.g., FDA food and beverage regulation).
markets.title: Will 3 mg THC beverages be federally legal to sell on Nov 16, 2026?

markets.rules_primary: If, as of 11:59 PM ET on Nov 13, 2026, federal law treats a hemp-derived beverage intended for human ingestion containing 3 milligrams or more of Total THC per Container as lawful hemp excluded from the Controlled Substances Act definition of marihuana rather than as a Schedule I controlled substance, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The determinative question is whether the 3-milligram Total THC level qualifies as lawful hemp under federal controlled-substance law at 11:59 PM ET on the Resolution Date. FDA food-safety, labeling, or other regulation outside the Controlled Substances Act does not by itself affect resolution, and state law does not affect resolution. Total THC is measured under the federal statutory standard in effect at the relevant time: delta-9 THC plus 0.877 times THCA, plus any other THC isomers included in the applicable federal statutory measure. 

A legally effective federal regime that leaves or makes a beverage containing 3 milligrams of Total THC per Container lawful hemp may resolve the market Yes, including continuation of the pre-Section 781 hemp definition, enacted federal legislation, a final federal regulation carrying the force of law, or nationwide federal court relief blocking enforcement of Section 781 of Public Law 119-37. Proposed or unenacted legislation or rules, informal federal non-enforcement or enforcement discretion, state action, and court relief limited to particular plaintiffs, products, sellers, or districts do not qualify. 

Only statutes, regulations, and court orders issued and legally effective by 11:59 PM ET on the Resolution Date are considered. An instrument whose operative provisions take effect only after that time does not qualify. Later corrections, amendments, or court decisions do not change resolution, even if they purport to apply retroactively. If no qualifying condition is in effect at the snapshot, the market resolves No.
markets.title: Will 3 mg THC beverages qualify as hemp under federal law on Nov 13, 2026?
